primary_article.headline: Power struggle erupts in Trump’s White House as midterm losses loom
primary_article.reporting_basis: Article says reporting draws on interviews with 20 staffers, advisers and people close to the president; most were anonymous to discuss personnel maneuvering.
primary_article.bounded_paraphrase: It reports that some aides believe Chief of Staff Susie Wiles might step down after the midterms and that several figures are positioning for the job. Separately, the article says Wiles has given aides or allies no indication she plans to leave. This is reported expectation and speculation, not an announced resignation/removal or confirmed departure.
primary_article.official_response: White House spokesperson Danielle Alvarez rejected the anonymous-source account as selfish/opportunistic behavior and said Trump had assembled a strong, talented, united team focused on the agenda. This is the administration response, distinct from the reporting and not a specific Wiles tenure commitment.
